utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to illustrate a point, my client once explained a concept to me and he's a professor of mathematics. I respect that. If you put ten points in a certain space you can draw a curve through these points relatively freely because you only have ten points. But if you put ten points there, then the curve is defined fully and no one can draw a different curve. So that is what I'm getting at, Your Honours. That's my point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 10, the obligation to disclose those documents that are on the 65 ter list, Article (G), in the same way that the Prosecution had to disclose all its documents. Now, I'm addressing myself to all Defence counsel. I would like you to put all your documents in binders, those documents which you intend to adduce through your witnesses. These documents should figure on the 65 ter list. And let me add that it would be advisable for all these documents to be put in a sequential order and not in any order. Please put them in a chronological order, which means that we would have on a shelf the Prlic case, so many documents in a chronological order. And for Petkovic's Defence, all the documents in a chronological order. Now, so that we have an overall view of all the 65 ter (G) documents, this is an application which the Trial Chamber is making. Even if afterwards some of these documents are then put into special binders when the witnesses come to testify. In that case, you can put your documents in different binders. It could be dedicated to certain topics. For instance, if it's Prozor, you could talk about expulsions, people who have been detained, people who have been driven out. So the Chamber would like to have a hard copy version of all your documents, preferably translated, in certain cases not translated, but we would like these to be in binders and in a chronological order. Is this possible or impossible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I'm sure Ms. Tomanovic is listening to what you're saying, and my case manager is as well. They would be in a better place to answer that question because they deal with those details, although I would say that it is rather a Herculean task that you're asking us to perform. It was our expectation -- I don't know what our colleagues are doing, but it was our expectation for every witness to have the binders ready prior to the commencement of the trial. In other words, not wait but have all of it. I will have to get back to you on that, but certainly I think if it's doable, we'll do it. We did hire some extra staff just for this part of the case. Obviously we want to accommodate the Trial Chamber as much as possible, and if this helps, then we obviously will do whatever we can to do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course binders can be prepared, but there is, of course, an essential difference perhaps to the binders that the Prosecution provided prior to a specific witness giving evidence and the 65 ter (G) requirements. For example, in the Stojic case, I've mentioned, Your Honours, that we anticipate calling up to 30 witnesses. And so 30 summaries will be prepared and a chart about which counts of the indictment they will speak to. Your Honour, the binders, of course prior to a witness being called in the Stojic case, Your Honours will be provided with binders. But it's not anticipated that on the 31st of March you will be given binders in relation to each of these witnesses. You will be given exactly what is required under 65 ter (G) which are the summaries and the counts that they speak to. So of course when a witness gives evidence there may be additional documents that have arisen in the course of -- that are going to be put to a witness that have arisen in course, for example, of another accused's case. Witness binders will be prepared that will help Your Honours and will be properly organised, buts that's at a later stage and they will be done prior to the Stojic Defence case starting. On the 31st of March something quite different is going to be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I'd like this to be quite clear. As the Bench has the heavy duty to assess the time of the parties now, to assess the time and to make sure that we don't make a mistake, how can we allocate the time properly? We will have the witness statement, and we will have the list of exhibits which you intend to adduce through the witness, and then you have the documents. So if you have a witness for whom you have a summary, you have planned to have three hours, and we will see whether these three hours are justified, and we will look at the documents to see whether you have planned to have 10, 15, 20, or 30 documents adduced through these witnesses. What are these documents, and then we shall check to see whether we are not going over the same ground again, because as you know, we have an overall picture of the case given the thousands of documents you wish to adduce. So on that basis we will be able to determine how much time is needed, but in order to do so, we need to have the statement, and we need to have the exhibits to see where we stand, because if you ask to have three hours and then we realise that only one or two exhibits will be adduced through the witness, then we will say, well, three hours is too much time. This is why. And this is in your interest also. It is important for us to have all these documents, and then we will be able to do a very good job. Mrs. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I only wish to raise one point. Your question and this lack of clarity among us as to what we are supposed to do as regards this request, it can be linked to the previous issue of untranslated documents. It's true that all the Defence teams, I'm almost certain of it, once their Defence cases start, will have all the documents they need translated. However, this will evidently not happen on the 31st of March. For this reason, I am afraid that even were we to create hard copies of all these documents, and if you were to look at all the documents and on that basis establish whether we need this a time, you will not be able to do so because you will not have the translations. Along with our witness lists, we will submit the list of documents with a clear description of each document. From this description you will be able to see what we intend to do through each particular witness. We will give lists of all the documents we wish to tender with each particular witness. For this reason, I believe that the hard copies Your Honours would receive from us on the 31st of March, if not all the documents have been translated, you will not be able to use them in the way you intend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Just briefly, Your Honours. A year and a half ago 90 per cent of the witnesses that we were offering had their statements and signed statements and certified statements. They were ready. Now, in Zagreb, in Belgrade, and in Sarajevo, there are authorised organisations or agencies for translation. The registry need do nothing more than call up one of the authorised agencies, ask how much they charge per page, and send the documents to these agencies to be translated. So I can imagine everything in this Tribunal except that we go to trial without me being able to show the truth and the facts as I see them on the basis of documents, because each of these witnesses are witnesses of what I claim to be true. With respect to details, the essential details, the psychosocial facts, the circumstances on the ground, what happened there, and so on and so forth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Let me remind you that the Trial Chamber started dealing with this a few -- several months ago, on the 27th of September, 2007. We issued a Scheduling Order in which we stated that the Defence was to prepare a list of the exhibits they want to show, and they also needed to say through which witness they intended to produce these documents. The Defence was also to disclose copies of these documents to the Prosecution with an English translation if need be. Six months ago we had already considered this. We had already planned this, and we had already asked you to do all this. Just as a reminder. Time has come to close this hearing. The Judges will meet on Wednesday. We'll review all your comments, and we'll rule and decide whether next week there will be or there will not be a 65 ter hearing. If we decide not to hold a hearing, the Chamber's legal officer will immediately send you a mail telling you that the hearing has been cancelled. Today we've covered practically all the items on the agenda. The Judges will now decide whether the -- next week's hearing has to be held. If we decide not to have a hearing next week, we'll meet again for The Pre-Defence Conference. Now, the question is whether we should push back that hearing or not, as Mr. Karnavas requested, and we'll tell you about our decision on that point. If you run into any types of problem, please let the Chamber's legal officer know about it. She's always available. Unless there is anything else crucial to deal with, I'll say that the hearing's adjourned. Yes. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll be very brief. Mr. Karnavas my colleague said that he didn't deal with technical matters so that he didn't know about that. Now, I do know about it because for the past two weeks I have helped my case manager with respect to technical issues, and I just have one case manager at my disposal faced with this situation, with the binders, the hard copy, the 65 ter list. We didn't count on that when we planned our work because when we started preparing the Defence case we set the amount of time needed for each matter to be attended to. Now, I'm -- I know how much time it takes to print out 2.000 documents and divide them up according to the witnesses, and if you want this to be done for all the witnesses then the same document might be shown to two or three witnesses which means we will have to copy it several times over, makes the situation far more complicated and I really do feel that we're not going to have enough time to hand over the 65 ter list on time because we thought -- I did think that we would have to provide hard copies, but we thought that this would be before our witness comes in, well before. And now I'm faced with this problem because I think that physically and technically I'm not able to be able to get through the 65 ter list, so I wanted to tell the Trial Chamber of that. Now, this principle of 200 pages per month applies to all the Defence teams and all the accused equally, and our team has two translators on our team from outside, and still they're not able to get through all the translations. I'm not a translator myself so I don't know how much time it takes, but I do know that with the help of these two translators we still haven't got through all the material. I don't know whether there was any misunderstanding when you asked whether you -- when you said what you wanted to have at your disposal, you mentioned statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm talking about the written statements, the written statements. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Ah, that relates then not to viva voce witnesses because we didn't take any statements from viva voce witnesses, just their summaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The summaries will do. That will be sufficient. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That's all I had to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Before we adjourn, the Trial Chamber will issue a number of decisions very shortly. Three or four of these decisions are on standby, but they will be handed down in the next few days. See you next time.
